question: When light is incident along the normal and passes from air to water, then the direction of light will __ __ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**not be changed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When light is incident along the normal to the surface between two media, it travels perpendicular to the interface.
 
• The direction of light does not change because the angle of incidence is 0 degrees, making the angle of refraction also 0 degrees.
 
• This phenomenon follows Snell's Law, where the refractive index difference does not cause bending if the light is incident normally.
 
• The speed of light will decrease as it enters water from air due to the higher refractive index of water, but its path remains unchanged.
 
• Such behavior is specific to light traveling along the normal; light incident at any other angle will undergo refraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Snell's Law**:

 
 
• Snell's Law states that n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂, where n is the refractive index of the medium and θ is the angle of incidence or refraction.
 
• When θ₁ = 0 (light incident normally), sinθ₁ = 0, making θ₂ also equal to 0.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**:
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another due to a change in its speed.
 
• It occurs only when the light strikes the boundary at an angle other than 0 degrees.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index**:
 
 
• The refractive index of air is approximately 1, while that of water is about 1.33.
 
• A higher refractive index indicates slower light speed in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Normal Incidence**:
 
 
• Normal incidence refers to light rays striking the surface perpendicularly (at an angle of 0 degrees).
 
• In this case, the light travels straight through without bending.
